section: Area Ratios Related to Side Length Ratios
subtopic: Area ratios with a shared angle
text: In the right triangle $\triangle ACE$, we have $AC = 12$, $CE = 16$, and $EA = 20$. Points $B$, $D$, and $F$ are located on $AC$, $CE$, and $EA$, respectively, so that $AB = 3$, $CD = 4$, and $EF = 5$. What is the ratio of the area of $\triangle DBF$ to that of $\triangle ACE$?
figure: Right triangle ACE with the right angle at C: A is at the top left, C at the bottom left and E at the bottom right, so AC is vertical and CE is horizontal (no right-angle mark is drawn). B is on AC with AB labeled 3 and BC labeled 9. D is on CE with CD labeled 4 and DE labeled 12. F is on the hypotenuse AE with AF labeled 15 and FE labeled 5. Segments BD, DF and FB are drawn, forming triangle DBF inside triangle ACE.
